newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends weak but off low as Brent steadies.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends weak but off low as Brent steadies.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended weaker but in the middle of a narrow range, helped off early lows by a modest recovery in Brent crude futures, brokers said.
Sept gas oil settled at $171.50 a tonne, down $2.25 from Thursday's close but above the intraday low of $170.00.

Dealers said gas oil futures were pulled up in late dealing by an upturn in crude, which lifted the Oct Brent contract to $18.99 a barrel by 1645 GMT, down seven cents on the day but 16 cents above the low.
"The locals are trying to push Brent towards $19.05. If it can get above $19.00 it could take off again," said a broker.
A reversal on Sept NYMEX unleaded gasoline, which turned early losses into gains of 0.27 cent a gallon to 66.60 cents was also helping crude higher, brokers said.
But a lack of volume, partly due to the absence of many European players due to the Assumption Day holiday, could foil a break to the upside.
"It's very difficult to generate any momentum because there's very little paper going through," said a broker.
Dealers said Brent was due to consolidate after rallying from $18.40 a barrel at Monday's open and some saw signs that the summer gasoline season may be beginning to falter.
Gasoline has proved the main price support in recent weeks with tight U.S. markets drawing product out of Europe and helping keep refinery margins strong.

Others said news of lower North Sea loadings -- the eight main exports systems are expected to pump 280,000 barrels per day (bpd) fewer next month than in August -- was providing some fundamental support to counter renewed Iraqi exports.
